speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: asked	the Minister for Communications and Information (a) what is the frequency of incidents involving the cutting of telecommunication cables by contractors carrying out earthworks; and (b) what steps are being taken to reduce such occurrences.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Of the 18, one was caused by 	Page: 23 contractors hired by a telecommunications operator (telco).

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The Infocomm Development Authority of Singapore (IDA) takes a serious view of all cable cut incidents.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Such incidents result in significant disruptions to telecommunication and media services delivered to our homes and businesses, causing great inconvenience to thousands of subscribers for many hours.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IDA's investigations revealed that most, if not all, of these cable cut incidents could have been avoided if contractors had exercised due diligence and caution when undertaking road works and construction projects.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These contractors failed to comply with clearly established standard operating procedures (SOPs), such as ascertaining the location of telecommunication cables prior to commencing earthworks and protecting underground cables against damage when they carried out their earthworks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In 16 of these cases, the service plans and cable detection reports obtained by the contractors clearly indicated the presence of telecommunication cables.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In the remaining two cases, the contractors did not obtain the necessary service plans and engage cable detection workers to detect the cables.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: They have to: first, give seven or more days' notice to the relevant telcos before the proposed earthworks; second, obtain information on the location of telecommunication cables and consult the operators on appropriate steps to prevent possible cable damage while the earthworks are being carried out; and finally, engage licensed telecommunication cable detection workers to detect such cables so that contractors can avoid these cables when carrying out their work.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Given the rise in the number of cable cut incidents, IDA is doing more.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is working closely with public agencies and telcos on preventive measures.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I understand that our telcos operators have agreed to advise contractors on the type of earthworks that should be avoided and the additional procedures to adhere to before and during earthworks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These include digging "trial holes" to locate any cables in the vicinity before commencing any earthworks and to contact the relevant telcos should they encounter any difficulty in locating the cables.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IDA has also been participating in regular dialogue sessions held by agencies, such as the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and the Energy Market Authority (EMA), with their contractors.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These sessions are meant to educate the contractors on the established SOPs and the precautionary measures needed to prevent a cable from being cut.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These measures will help facilitate the detection of new underground 	Page: 24 telecommunication cables and, hopefully, reduce the occurrence of cable cuts.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: My Ministry and IDA will continue to work closely with other public agencies to reduce the frequency of such cuts.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I wish to emphasise that the parties involved in road works or construction projects must also adopt the necessary precautions to avoid such incidents.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Only through a concerted effort by all relevant parties can cable cut incidents be avoided.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: On the second question, as mentioned in my reply, the range of fines determined by the Court is from $60,000 to $570,000.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In fact, we have worked with all the operators to make sure that they can avoid such an incident.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The largest area we know of is probably in some parts of the areas in the northwest of Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: By and large, the most important thing is that the telcos have remediation programmes in place to make sure that we can minimise the disruption.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: At the end of the day, if we can minimise the cable cuts, then we do not have to deal with all these problems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We know that our underground is getting congested and, therefore, we need to work with the agencies and, more importantly, to educate the contractors that they have to take due diligence to avoid such an incident.
